# OmniReel

**One prompt in. One ~120-second film out — assembled from short clips generated by several independent AI video providers, using only free allowances.**

OmniReel is a lightweight controller. Every frame is generated on a remote API; your machine only plans, schedules, downloads and joins the results with FFmpeg. Nothing is inferred locally, so it runs comfortably on an old laptop.

```
prompt ──► storyboard planner ──► scene timeline (dynamic 4–12 s segments)
                                        │
                                        ▼
                         multi-provider scheduler ── quota ledger
                          │        │        │              │
                       Agnes    Replicate   …      health + failover
                          │        │        │
                          └────────┴────────┘
                                   ▼
                     clips on disk ──► FFmpeg ──► final.mp4 (~120 s)
```

## Why this exists

Individual free video models produce 4–12 second clips and come with small allowances. Asking one provider for two uninterrupted minutes is not possible. OmniReel treats those short clips as **building blocks**, not deliverables:

* one creative prompt becomes a complete, timed storyboard;
* every shot's length is chosen from what the available models can actually generate;
* different providers generate different scenes, so no single free allowance is drained;
* when a provider refuses, rate-limits or errors, **only that scene** moves to another provider;
* finished scenes are never thrown away, and the project resumes after restarts;
* FFmpeg joins everything into one continuous film, validated with `ffprobe`.

The default target is 120 seconds. Twelve 10-second clips, twenty 6-second clips and twenty-four 5-second clips are all legal — the planner solves whichever timeline is reachable.

## Features

**Planning**
- Rule-based storyboard engine with eleven visual styles and a twelve-beat narrative arc
- Exact timeline solving: shot lengths come from the capability registry, not a constant
- Editable storyboard: every scene's prompt, camera and lighting can be changed before spending a call

**Scheduling**
- Three independent free sources enabled by default — Agnes, Zhipu CogVideoX-Flash and ModelScope — so one provider resting does not stall a two-minute project
- Persistent quota ledger (daily windows, trial credits, promotional expiry, per-key rate limits)
- Provider health with circuit breaking and exponential backoff
- Four generation modes: `free_max` (default), `balanced`, `best_quality`, `preferred`
- Soft per-model cap so one model cannot swallow a whole project when alternatives exist
- Scene-level failover and per-scene manual pinning

**Continuity**
- World bible (subject, palette, grade, lighting) injected into every shot prompt
- Previous clip's final frame extracted and passed as a keyframe/reference where the model supports it
- Provider changes never change the creative direction

**Recovery**
- SQLite-backed jobs, attempts, quota and remote job ids
- Restart mid-project: completed clips stay, in-flight jobs keep polling, pending scenes dispatch
- `waiting` projects resume automatically when a provider recovers

**Assembly**
- Per-clip normalisation (resolution, fps, pixel format, audio), then concat with stream copy
- Optional crossfades, optional background music, optional offline narration (Piper/espeak-ng)
- Final duration validated with `ffprobe`; the assembled film is copied next to the per-scene clips

## Quick start (Linux Mint / Ubuntu)

```bash
git clone <your-fork-url> omnireel
cd omnireel
./scripts/install.sh              # venv, backend deps, frontend build, .env
nano .env                         # set BIGMODEL_API_KEY (free) or AGNES_API_KEY
./scripts/run.sh                  # http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

Prove the machine works before spending a call — a 20-second film takes seconds:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/smoke_run.py --seconds 20 --expect 20
```

That runs the whole chain (storyboard → scheduler → providers → FFmpeg) with the offline mock provider and real FFmpeg, and **fails unless the finished MP4 measures 20 s**. `--minutes 2` does the same at full length. Mock clips are labelled colour cards, never AI footage.

Once a key is in `.env`, the same command makes a genuine film, and 20 seconds costs only two calls:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/smoke_run.py --seconds 20 --live
```

Start there rather than at two minutes: a stuck model costs you two calls, not twenty-four.

See the plan before paying for it — this makes no API call at all:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/smoke_run.py --seconds 20 --dry-run --live \
  --prompt "A red fox trots through a snowy pine forest at dusk, stops, and looks straight at the camera"
```

It prints the clip lengths your configuration makes available, then every scene's duration, prompt, camera and lighting. `--prompt` and `--style` work the same way on a real run.

### What the CI artifact is — and is not

Every push to `main` renders a 20-second film and uploads it as **`pipeline-test-mock-20s-not-ai-footage`**. Those frames come from the mock provider: flat colour cards carrying a text slate with the scene number, length and prompt. They prove the timeline solver, the scheduler, the download path and the FFmpeg join on real files. **They are not AI footage.** If you open that MP4 expecting a film, you will see a coloured card with writing on it — that is the whole point of it, and the name now says so.

### Get a real film from your phone

No terminal, no local install — GitHub runs it:

1. Get a free key at [bigmodel.cn](https://bigmodel.cn). CogVideoX-Flash is priced 免费 and needs no card.
2. In this repository: **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret**, name it `BIGMODEL_API_KEY`, paste the key.
3. **Actions → Live 20 second film → Run workflow**, type your prompt, press Run.
4. When it finishes, download the **`REAL-AI-film`** artifact: the MP4, a contact sheet, and the per-scene clips.

The workflow prints the storyboard into the run log *before* spending a call, so you can see the scenes and their prompts first. `AGNES_API_KEY` or `MODELSCOPE_API_TOKEN` work in place of the BigModel key.

At 20 seconds this is two API calls. Start there, not at 120.

Full instructions: [INSTALLATION.md](INSTALLATION.md). Keys and endpoints: [API_CONFIGURATION.md](API_CONFIGURATION.md).

## Provider status — read this before expecting free footage

| Provider | Models | Status in OmniReel | Free? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Agnes AI** | Video 2.5 Flash | **Fully implemented and verified.** `POST /v1/videos`, poll `/v1/videos/{id}`, `metadata.url` on completion. 4–12 s clips, 720p. | Recurring free with a ~16 req/min ceiling |
| **Zhipu BigModel** | CogVideoX-Flash | **Implemented and verified from vendor docs.** `POST /api/paas/v4/videos/generations`, poll `/async-result/{id}`, `video_result[0].url`. | **Recurring free** — priced 免费. Clip length is service-chosen |
| **ModelScope** | MiniMax H3 | **Implemented and verified from vendor docs.** `POST /v1/videos/generations`, poll `/v1/tasks/{id}`. 3/5/10 s. | Free, credit-metered from a daily 魔粒 wallet |
| **Pollinations** | 28 models: Veo 3.1, Kling 3.0, Seedance, WAN, LTX, MiniMax, Grok | Implemented (async job flow). One key, every major hosted model, including the only 15 s clip here. | **No** — every video model is `paid_only` |
| **Replicate** | MiniMax Video-01 | Implemented (official predictions API). 6 s clips. | Trial runs only, then billed |
| **Hugging Face** | WAN 2.2 T2V | Implemented (synchronous bytes). | Pay-as-you-go / PRO credits |
| **Runware** | any video model | Implemented against its task API; **model id must be confirmed in your dashboard**. | One-off startup credits |
| **YepAPI-style gateway** | your models | Configurable template — you supply base URL and paths. | One-off credits |
| **mock** | mock-video | Test/demo only, never AI footage. | n/a |

Details, sources and verification dates: [PROVIDER_RESEARCH.md](PROVIDER_RESEARCH.md) and [MODEL_COMPATIBILITY.md](MODEL_COMPATIBILITY.md). OmniReel never invents a quota: unpublished numbers are shown as *estimated* and providers that cannot be verified ship disabled.

## How the two-minute film is actually built

1. `POST /api/projects` with one prompt → planner produces N scenes summing to the target.
2. `POST /api/projects/{id}/start` → worker begins.
3. Per scene: rank candidates (capability → free eligibility → health → quota → score), submit, poll, download, validate.
4. On failure: refund the ledger, cool the provider, retry **the same scene** on the next candidate.
5. When every scene is ready: FFmpeg normalises, joins, trims to target, validates → `data/outputs/<project>.mp4`.

The scheduler keeps at most two remote jobs in flight by default, which keeps the old laptop cool and stays inside most per-minute limits.

## Repository layout

```
backend/
  omnireel/
    planner.py        storyboard + exact timeline solving
    capabilities.py   model catalogue (durations, resolutions, free status)
    scheduler.py      ranking, submission, failover, download
    quota.py          quota ledger + provider health
    worker.py         persistent generation loop
    assembly.py       FFmpeg plan + execution
    continuity.py     frame extraction, ffprobe helpers
    audio.py          offline narration
    providers/        agnes, bigmodel, modelscope, pollinations,
                      replicate, huggingface, runware, yepapi, mock
    api.py            FastAPI surface
  tests/              planner, quota, scheduler, worker, assembly, API, providers
frontend/             React + Vite studio
scripts/              install, run, dev, smoke_run, discover_models
config/               provider override example
data/                 runtime: db, clips, frames, outputs (git-ignored)
```

## Honest limitations

- **Free tiers change without notice.** If Agnes rotates its model names or durations, update `capabilities.py` or `config/providers.json` and re-check the provider's console.
- **No adapter has completed a live run yet.** Agnes, Zhipu BigModel, ModelScope and Pollinations are verified from vendor documentation — and, for Pollinations, from its live model registry. The rest are real HTTP implementations whose model ids and free grants must be confirmed in your account before enabling.
- **Clip lengths are guesses when providers are vague.** `cogvideox-flash` is the extreme case: its request schema has no duration field at all, so 5 s is a planning assumption. Requested vs actual duration is recorded per scene; assembly trims to the target and reports any shortfall instead of hiding it.
- **Continuity is best-effort.** Providers that accept a first-frame image get a real keyframe; the rest only get prompt-level consistency, which is weaker.
- **Quality is model-limited.** Two minutes stitched from several models will have different "looks" between providers — that is the price of free multi-provider generation.
- **This is not a render farm.** The controller is deliberately tiny; a 2-core i3 handles 120 s of 720p assembly in well under a minute.
